item2.title: Flatmates

item3.title: Dinners and rounds

item4.title: Remote crews

item1.title: Free forever

item2.title: No account needed
item2.body: No email, no password, no ID checks. The link is the key — keep it in the group.

item3.title: Settle however you like
item3.body: Cash, bank transfer, or whatever app you already use. We just record it.

remembered.title: Opened rooms stay on this device
remembered.body: Split keeps them in the list on this page so you can return from here.

money.title: Split keeps the maths, not the money
money.body: It records who paid and who owes. You settle wherever you already pay.

readMore.toggleHint: Who made Split, why it’s free forever, and how room links work.

join.title: What your friends see
join.body: One tap and a name. No email, no password, nothing to download — what you are asking of them is smaller than what you are asking of yourself.

currency.title: 162 supported currencies
currency.body: The room counts in one currency. Add an expense in any of the 162 supported currencies and Split converts it at the rate on the day.

splits.title: Splits that are not even
splits.body: Equal, by shares, by exact amounts, or with some people left out of a line.

exact.title: Reconciles to the cent
exact.body: Balances always sum to zero, and you can open any balance to see exactly how it was reached.

live.title: Everyone sees it at once
live.body: Add something on the bus and it is on everyone else’s screen before you get off.

offline.title: Works with no signal
offline.body: Type an expense in a basement or up a mountain. It waits on your phone and goes when the signal comes back.

home.title: Add it to your home screen

transfers.title: A simpler payment plan
transfers.body: Split turns a web of balances into a short suggested list of who should pay whom.

settle.title: How you get paid back
settle.body: Split tells you who should pay whom. You send the money the way you already would, and the room records that you did.

team.title: The people who built it
team.intro: Split has no users yet, so there is nobody to quote but us.

konrad.name: Konrad
konrad.quote: Every trip ended the same way: a spreadsheet nobody updated, and one person quietly out of pocket.

hugo.name: Hugo
hugo.quote: I wanted the whole thing to be a link. If your friends have to make an account, they will not.

who.title: Who made this, and why it is free forever

built.title: Peanut built Split
built.body: Peanut is a payments app and a real company with a real product — not a weekend project that disappears.

free.title: It is free forever because it introduces people to Peanut
free.body: No premium tier, no upsell coming, nothing to buy.

data.title: There is not much here to leak
data.body: Room links are kept out of our own analytics, because a link is a key.

retype.q: Do I have to retype everything from the group chat?
retype.a: For a trip that already happened, yes — the expenses get typed in once. It is lighter than it sounds, because everyone in the room can add their own instead of it all landing on you.
retype.import: If you are coming from Splitwise, the import page brings a whole group across in one step.

access.a: Anyone with the link. It is kept out of search engines and cannot be guessed, but it is a key — keep it in the group chat rather than anywhere public.

lost.q: How do we get back to the room?
lost.a: Leave the link in the group chat so everyone can find it there. Split also saves rooms you open on this device, and you can paste the link on the home page to add it back.

limits.q: Is there a limit on how many expenses we can add?
limits.a: No. Add fifty in an afternoon if that is the kind of trip it is.

existing.repeatBody: After an import is completed on this screen, submitting the exact same reviewed source data here changes nothing, even if you change the people mapping. Expenses already in the room may not have a matching import record, so the first append can repeat them. A changed export is added in full. If it overlaps earlier history, those expenses can appear twice because source exports have calendar dates, not stable expense IDs.

fx.title: About the exchange rates
fx.body: This group spent in more than one currency. Splitwise does not export the rate it used on the day, so everything is converted at today’s rate — the totals will be close, not identical to the ones you see there.

warnings.ROW_BAD_AMOUNT: Row {row} has an amount we could not read, so it was left out.
warnings.ROW_BAD_DATE: Row {row} has a date we could not read — it comes in dated today.
warnings.ROW_DESCRIPTION_TRUNCATED: Row {row} has a very long description — it comes in shortened.
warnings.ROW_CATEGORY_TRUNCATED: Row {row} has a very long category — it comes in shortened.
warnings.MEMBER_NAME_TRUNCATED: One name was too long and comes in shortened, as “{detail}”. You can edit it above.
warnings.MULTI_PAYER_SPLIT: “{detail}” was paid by more than one person. The file does not record who put in what, so it arrives as one expense per payer — the balances are exact, the split between payers is our best reading.
warnings.PAYMENT_ROWS: Payments between people arrive as expenses rather than as settled-up records. The balances come out the same.
warnings.DUPLICATE_MEMBER_NAME: Two people are called {detail}, so the second is listed as “{detail} (2)”. Rename them below.
warnings.TRUNCATED_HISTORY: A room holds 500 expenses, so the {count, plural, one {# oldest one} other {# oldest ones}} arrive as a single “Balance brought forward” entry per person instead. Everyone's balance still comes out the same.
warnings.SPLITPRO_BALANCES_ONLY: Split Pro’s account download contains current balances, but not expense history. They arrive as “Balance brought forward” entries, so everyone’s total is preserved but the old expense list is not.
warnings.SPLITPRO_PAIR_HISTORY: Split Pro’s friend CSV does not say which group each expense belonged to. Every expense in this file arrives together in this room.
warnings.SPLITPRO_MISSING_NAMES: Split Pro left {count, plural, one {one person’s name} other {# people’s names}} out of the backup. They are labelled “Member” below — rename them before creating the room.
warnings.SPLITPRO_BALANCES_SKIPPED: {count, plural, one {One balance in the Split Pro backup is incomplete, so it was left out} other {# balances in the Split Pro backup are incomplete, so they were left out}}. Compare the preview with Split Pro before creating the room.
warnings.SPLITPRO_UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY: Split cannot convert {detail}, so balances in that currency were left out. Choose another export if those balances matter.

errors.NOT_SPLITWISE_CSV: We don’t recognize this file. Choose a Splitwise group .csv, a Split Pro friend .csv, or the splitpro_data.json file from Split Pro’s Account page.
errors.MALFORMED_JSON: That JSON file is incomplete or damaged. Download “SplitPro data” again from Split Pro’s Account page and use the new file without editing it.
errors.SPLITPRO_DIRECT_UNRESOLVED: This Split Pro backup does not identify which member is you, so balances outside named groups cannot be separated safely. Import the groups above, then use each friend’s CSV export for any remaining balance.
errors.NO_MEMBERS: This export does not contain a group roster. In Splitwise, export a group; in Split Pro, use “Download SplitPro data” from the Account page.
errors.NO_EXPENSES: There is nothing this file can bring across. The group may already be settled, or every balance may use an unsupported currency. Check the balances in the source app, then create an empty room if they are all zero.
errors.TOO_MANY_MEMBERS: This group has more than 20 people. Remove inactive people in the source app and export it again, or create two smaller rooms.
errors.TOO_MANY_EXPENSES: This export is too large to process safely. Export a smaller group or use a Split Pro account backup, which brings over current balances instead of every old expense.
errors.FILE_TOO_BIG: This file is over the 1 MB import limit. Export one Splitwise group, or download a fresh Split Pro account backup and try that file.
errors.READ_FAILED: Your browser could not read this file. Download a fresh export, keep it as .csv or .json, and try the new copy.
errors.DUPLICATE_NAMES: Two people have the same name — make them different so every expense lands on the right person.
errors.failed: The room could not be created. Check your connection and try again; nothing was imported.
